title: Use functions to make reliable quotes
outcome: Calculate a price using one reusable, tested set of rules.
story: Different staff members are quoting different prices for the same order. Amina wants one clear calculation everyone can use.

frames.explanation: The same inputs produce the same quote.
The function also owns the rule for unacceptable input.

sections.title: Give a group of instructions a name
paragraphs: A function groups instructions so they can be reused. A quote function receives a price, quantity, and shipping cost, then returns an answer. Calling the function runs its instructions for the inputs you supply.

The values listed in the function definition are parameters. The values supplied in a call are arguments. A return instruction sends a result back to the caller. These words describe the inputs and output you already used in earlier lessons.

sections.title: Agree on a contract
paragraphs: A contract states what inputs a function accepts and what it returns. Our quote accepts a whole-number price in cents, a positive whole-number quantity, and a non-negative shipping cost. It returns items, discount, and total.

A function should reject inputs outside that contract rather than produce a plausible-looking price. We use throw new RangeError to report unacceptable numbers. The caller can catch that error and explain it to the person using the app.

sections.title: Keep money exact
paragraphs: Use integer cents for this exercise. A price of 200 cents is two units of currency with one hundred cents per unit. Adding and multiplying whole-number cents avoids common decimal-fraction surprises.

The shop’s fictional rule is a 10% item discount for quantities of five or more. Round the discount down to a whole cent using Math.floor(items / 10). Add shipping after subtracting the discount. Real products must agree on their currency and rounding policy.

sections.title: Separate the rule from the screen
paragraphs: The quote function should not read a text box or draw a button. Its job is calculation and validation. An interface can collect input and display the returned result. A backend can reuse the same contract while obtaining prices from an authoritative catalogue.

A small function is easier to test because we can call it with several inputs without opening the whole application. Good boundaries also make change safer: a new screen need not invent a new pricing rule.

words.meaning: A named group of instructions that can receive inputs and return a result.
The agreed rules for acceptable inputs and the result.
Send a result back to whoever called the function.

return sends their product back to the caller.
The call supplies 200 and 3. Another call can reuse the instructions with different numbers.

exercise.title: A shared order quote
exercise.brief: Write quote(priceCents, quantity, shippingCents). Return { items, discount, total }. Reject unacceptable inputs using RangeError.

steps.title: Calculate items and shipping
steps.task: Multiply price by quantity. Add shipping to get the total. Keep discount at zero for now.
steps.hint: Name the intermediate amount items so the return object is easy to explain.

steps.title: Enforce the input contract
steps.task: Reject non-whole numbers, negative prices or shipping, and quantities below one.
steps.hint: Validate all three inputs before multiplying. Throw new RangeError("Invalid quote input") on failure.

steps.title: Apply the agreed discount
steps.task: For quantities of five or more, subtract Math.floor(items / 10). Keep shipping outside the discount.
steps.hint: Use quantity >= 5 ? Math.floor(items / 10) : 0 to choose the discount.

cases.why: Use the stated rounding policy rather than an accidental decimal result.

project.title: A reliable quote desk
project.brief: Build a reusable quote function and a small catalogue of examples. Another developer should be able to call it without reading the implementation.
deliverables: An explanation of currency units and rounding.

milestones.title: Write the contract
actions: Name the units for every price.
List valid input ranges and output fields.

milestones.title: Implement the rules
actions: Add validation and the quantity discount.

milestones.title: Review the boundaries
actions: Test quantities of four and five.
Test a fractional-cent discount and rejected inputs.

acceptance: All money values use integer cents.
The discount boundary and rounding policy are tested.
A caller can understand every output field.
project.extension: Add a second delivery option using a separate function. Keep catalogue prices controlled by the shop.
reflection: Why separate calculation from the interface?
Which rounding decision did you make explicit?
